about.title: Fortuna Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Fortuna is a small town of about 12,000 people, and losing someone here is rarely an anonymous event. Neighbors on Main Street notice. Coworkers on Rohnerville Road ask how you are holding up. In the middle of that grief, the practical side of a death caused by someone else's carelessness can feel impossible to face. A wrongful death claim in California is a civil action, separate from any criminal case, brought by a spouse or domestic partner, children, or sometimes other dependents and heirs. It can cover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Fortuna's public collision records for 2025 show two injury crashes and no traffic deaths, and that matters: wrongful death claims here often begin somewhere other than a roadway, such as a workplace, a medical setting, or an unsafe property. LawProactive is free to use. We connect Humboldt County families with an independent attorney who reviews the situation and, if you choose to move forward, works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Fortuna Families Start With LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: The two-year clock is watched
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Connecting early keeps those deadlines from slipping by while you grieve.

items.title: Every recoverable loss is considered
items.desc: Funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance are all part of a California claim. The attorney you are matched with works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Fortuna recorded zero traffic deaths in 2025. Do wrongful death claims still happen here?
items.answer: Yes. Traffic collisions are only one way a family can lose someone to negligence, and in a town of Fortuna's size the cause is often a workplace accident, a medical error, or an unsafe condition on private property. The legal standard is the same regardless of how the death occurred. If another person or business failed to act with reasonable care, a civil claim may be available.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges in Humboldt County. Can we still bring a civil claim?
items.answer: You can. A wrongful death case is a separate civil action, and it does not depend on whether prosecutors file charges or win a conviction. The civil case focuses on your family's losses rather than punishment. Some families choose to wait for the criminal matter to develop, but the two-year deadline still applies, so it helps to get advice early.

items.question: What if a city or county vehicle or property was involved in the death?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California follow a much shorter timeline than the standard two years, and a formal claim usually has to be presented before a lawsuit can be filed. Missing that step can end the case before it starts. An independent attorney can tell you quickly whether a public entity is involved and what has to happen first.
